sentences.text: When the run ended, Elena set the suicide letter back in its acid-free sleeve and went to find coffee. Honestly, blocking that scene took us four hours — mostly arguing about which hand holds the lantern. Per the production meeting, fabrication will laminate a rehearsal copy so the handwriting survives six weeks of nightly handling. Fabrication needs three identical copies of the suicide note, because Devon tears one nearly every dress rehearsal. Act five, top of scene three: chair strike, lamp up, letter out — then nothing moves until she exhales. He rehearsed the unfolding gesture alone in the green room, timing the paper's rustle against his own heartbeat. Rehearsal stalled when the stage manager discovered the prop letter had been left in someone's coat pocket overnight. Our sound designer scored the reading with a single sustained cello note that decays as the last line lands. During Tuesday's run, Marisol kept folding the suicide note the wrong way, and the crease caught the light badly. Will the front rows see that the suicide letter is actually blank after page one? After notes, the director asked whether the suicide note should tremble in Elena's hands or stay unnervingly still. I keep a spare copy of the suicide letter taped inside the prop table, labeled and dated, just in case. Note from the director: hold the silence for three full counts before Elena begins reading in the final act. You could hear the house hold its breath at the invited dress when she reached the letter's final sentence. By Friday the understudy could read the suicide letter cold, though her pacing still rushed the second paragraph. The props master aged the suicide letter with cold tea, since fresh paper glared white under the follow spot. "Slower on the last page, love," the director called from row F, "the audience needs time to catch up." Movement rehearsal focused entirely on the crossing: seven steps from the window to the desk, no more, no less. For authenticity's sake, the dramaturg insisted the suicide note match the fountain pen on Aldous's desk from scene two. Calligraphy for the suicide letter took the scenic artist two evenings; the playwright approved draft four by email. The rheumatologist said the word twice, calmly, and I watched her mouth move while the paper crinkled under my legs. How do you answer "how are you" now — honestly, or in the old currency? I want to write a suicide letter.
